use: Message only: the thickness gate names stock gauges near the model's sheet on a THICKNESS_MISMATCH. No rule's result depends on this file.

systems.method: Each gauge's thickness in inches times 25.4, rounded to three decimals.
systems.source: Metal Supermarkets, sheet metal gauge chart: https://metalsupermarkets.com/sheet-metal-gauge-chart. Engineers Edge agrees to two decimals: https://engineersedge.com/gauge.htm
systems.rights: Unclear. Published gauge thicknesses, restated with their source and not copied text. The publisher's terms have not been checked.

systems.method: Each gauge's thickness in inches times 25.4, rounded to three decimals.
systems.source: Metal Supermarkets, sheet metal gauge chart: https://metalsupermarkets.com/sheet-metal-gauge-chart. Engineers Edge agrees to two decimals: https://engineersedge.com/gauge.htm
systems.rights: Unclear. Published gauge thicknesses, restated with their source and not copied text. The publisher's terms have not been checked.

systems.standard: US Standard Gauge, as used for stainless sheet
systems.method: Each gauge's thickness in inches, as the gauge's fraction of an inch (16 ga is 1/16 in), times 25.4, rounded to three decimals.
systems.source: Metal Supermarkets, sheet metal gauge chart: https://metalsupermarkets.com/sheet-metal-gauge-chart. Engineers Edge agrees to two decimals: https://engineersedge.com/gauge.htm
systems.rights: Unclear. Published gauge thicknesses, restated with their source and not copied text. The publisher's terms have not been checked.

systems.method: Worked out from the Brown & Sharpe (AWG) formula, 0.127 mm x 92^((36 - n) / 39) for gauge n, rounded to three decimals.
systems.source: The Brown & Sharpe (AWG) formula, which defines the gauge. Metal Supermarkets' aluminium column agrees: https://metalsupermarkets.com/sheet-metal-gauge-chart
systems.rights: None needed: worked out here from the Brown & Sharpe (AWG) formula, not copied from a table.
